value.behaviour: jsdom tests for the unread notifications card: rendering and links, empty state, mark-as-read, signal-triggered refresh, and the polling fallback with its cleanup.
rules: Apache header with 2026. Imports: act, fireEvent, screen from '@testing-library/react'; renderInTestApp, TestApiProvider from '@backstage/test-utils'; toastApiRef from '@backstage/frontend-plugin-api'; signalApiRef from '@backstage/plugin-signals-react'; Notification from '@backstage/plugin-notifications-common'; notificationsApiRef from '../../api'; rootRouteRef from '../../routes'; UnreadNotificationsCard from './UnreadNotificationsCard'.
A helper makeNotification(id, title) returns a Notification with user 'user:default/guest', origin 'test', created new Date(), payload { title, severity: 'normal' }.

Mock the notifications API as { getNotifications: jest.fn(), updateNotifications: jest.fn() } using mockResolvedValueOnce chains of { notifications, totalCount } so each refetch can return a different list; updateNotifications resolves [].

Every render wraps UnreadNotificationsCard in TestApiProvider with at least [notificationsApiRef, api] and [toastApiRef, { post: jest.fn() }], and passes renderInTestApp the option mountedRoutes: { '/notifications': rootRouteRef }.
Wait for content with screen.findByText or findByRole only; no waitFor, no test ids; signal deliveries and timer advances run inside act.
The polling test calls jest.useFakeTimers() before rendering and jest.useRealTimers() at its end; an afterEach also calls jest.useRealTimers() and jest.clearAllMocks().

tests.name: renders the title, unread items with deep links and the view all link
tests.given: getNotifications resolves two notifications with ids 'n1' and 'n2' and titles 'First alert' and 'Second alert'
tests.expect: findByText('Unread notifications') is present; getNotifications was called with an object containing read false and limit 5; 'First alert' is inside a link whose href ends with '/notifications?id=n1' and 'Second alert' inside one ending with '/notifications?id=n2'; a link named 'View all notifications' has href '/notifications'; two buttons are named 'Mark as read'

tests.name: shows the empty state when there are no unread notifications
tests.expect: findByText('No unread notifications') is present and no 'Mark as read' button exists

tests.name: marks an item as read and refetches the list
tests.given: getNotifications first resolves 'n1' and 'n2', then resolves only 'n2'
tests.expect: after fireEvent.click on the first 'Mark as read' button, updateNotifications was called with { ids: ['n1'], read: true }; findByText('Second alert') resolves after the refetch, queryByText('First alert') is null, and getNotifications was called twice

tests.name: refetches when a notifications signal arrives and unsubscribes on unmount
tests.given: a signal API whose subscribe is a jest.fn storing the callback and returning { unsubscribe: jest.fn() }; getNotifications first resolves 'n1', then resolves 'n1' and 'n3' titled 'Third alert'
tests.expect: subscribe was called with 'notifications'; after act calls the stored callback with { action: 'new_notification', notification_id: 'n3' }, findByText('Third alert') resolves and getNotifications was called twice; after unmount the unsubscribe mock was called once

tests.name: polls when signals are unavailable and stops polling after unmount
tests.given: no signal API, fake timers, pollingIntervalMs 1000 (below the 10 s minimum), getNotifications resolving 'n1' every time
tests.expect: after the first render getNotifications was called once; advancing timers by 9000 ms inside act adds no call; advancing by another 1000 ms makes it called twice; after unmount, advancing by 60000 ms leaves it at two calls

rules: Apache header with 2026. Imports: screen from '@testing-library/react'; renderInTestApp, TestApiProvider from '@backstage/test-utils'; toastApiRef from '@backstage/frontend-plugin-api'; Notification from '@backstage/plugin-notifications-common'; notificationsApiRef from '../../api'; NotificationsPage from './NotificationsPage'.

Mock the notifications API with getNotifications resolving { notifications: [n1 'First alert', n2 'Second alert'], totalCount: 2 }, getStatus resolving { unread: 2, read: 0 }, getTopics resolving { topics: [] }, updateNotifications resolving []; also provide [toastApiRef, { post: jest.fn() }].
Render <NotificationsPage /> inside TestApiProvider with renderInTestApp and the option routeEntries: ['/notifications?id=n2'] (or ['/notifications'] for the second case).
The highlighted marker is found with closest('[aria-current="true"]') from the title text; CSS modules map class names to themselves under jest, so the marked element has class 'highlighted'.
Use screen.findByText to wait for rows; no waitFor, no test ids.

tests.name: highlights the notification named in the id search parameter
tests.given: the page opened at '/notifications?id=n2' with two notifications n1 and n2
tests.expect: the element around 'Second alert' with aria-current 'true' exists and has class 'highlighted'; 'First alert' has no ancestor with aria-current, and only one element on the page has aria-current

tests.name: highlights nothing without an id search parameter
tests.given: the page opened at '/notifications' with the same two notifications
tests.expect: both titles render and no element has aria-current
